key_insight: Corner vortices in triangular cavity flow form a self-similar cascade with non-integer fractal dimensions, and their scaling can be estimated from vortex size and intensity ratios.
engineering_relevance: These fractal scaling laws help predict recirculation structure in slow viscous cavity flows, supporting better modeling of corner eddies in microfluidic, thermal, and CFD applications.
method: Solved the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in a triangular cavity using a pressure-based coupled solver.
Measured successive vortex size and intensity ratios to characterize the Moffatt vortex cascade.
Estimated fractal dimension with an area-perimeter approach and proposed an empirical relation for arbitrary grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing corner vortices with fractal dimensions between 1 and 2, plus a Reynolds-number study and a comparison against square-cavity self-similarity.
watch_item: The empirical fractal-dimension relation is tied to numerical resolution and cavity geometry, so it may need revalidation before transfer to different meshes or boundary conditions.
paper_title: Fractal Scaling of Moffatt Vortices in Triangular Cavity Flow
